第 69 章 Prioritize Building Relationships with Your Peers优先和同侪建立关系

Rocio Delgado / 罗西奥·德尔加多

— 第 194 页 —

When we become managers, we become responsible for the success of the team that we are leading. We immediately start building relationships with our direct reports, managing career development, removing blockers, providing context, helping set goals and resolving conflicts. We begin spending time in one-on-ones on a recurrent basis to get to know them, understand their drivers, and help them to grow and achieve their goals.

当我们成为经理时，我们对所领导团队的成功负责。我们立刻开始和下属建立关系、管理职业发展、移除阻碍、提供上下文、帮助设定目标和解决冲突。我们开始定期花时间在一对一上了解他们、理解他们的驱动力、帮他们成长和实现目标。

Although all of this is extremely important, it's critical to build similar relationships with your peers across the organization. Neglecting to do so contributes to the creation of silos, poor decision making, and potentially an "us versus them mentality," which causes collaboration problems between teams. As managers, our peers are our team #1 and not our direct reports. Team #1, as described by Patrick Lencioni, in his book Five Dysfunctions of a Team, refers to the team that is your priority. When a leader makes the team they're directly managing the priority over everything else, it's easy to forget that they are part of the larger organization and that they need alignment with peer teams to make sure they are working toward the proper set of goals.

虽然这些都极其重要，和组织里的同侪建立类似关系也至关重要。忽视这样做会导致孤岛、糟糕决策、以及可能的「我们对抗他们的心态」，造成团队间协作问题。作为经理，我们的同侪是我们的 1 号团队，不是下属。1 号团队，正如 Patrick Lencioni 在《团队的五种障碍》一书中描述的，指你的优先团队。当一个领导把直接管理的团队置于一切之上时，很容易忘记他们是更大组织的一部分，需要和同侪团队对齐以确保朝正确的目标集努力。

To be part of a cohesive organization, everyone should pay attention to the collective set of goals and results above the individual interest of the team they manage. This might sound counterintuitive or even feel disloyal, but think about it as an orchestra. If musicians of the string sections work in isolation from the percussion section, the music is not going to come out as it should, even if each musician is the best at what they do.

要成为有凝聚力组织的一部分，每个人都应该关注集体的目标和结果，高于他们管理团队的个人利益。这可能听起来反直觉甚至感觉不忠诚，但把它想成交响乐团。如果弦乐组的音乐家和打击乐组隔离工作，音乐不会像应该的那样出来，即使每个音乐家都是各自领域最好的。

— 第 195 页 —

Executive teams often apply this concept; however, it's applicable at any level. Whether you work in a product engineering team, infrastructure, SRE, or QA, you need to build relationships with the group of leaders with whom you collaborate. Together you will define priorities, schedule releases, develop a strategy for your products, and so on, and this collaboration is critical to your success and in consequence the success of the team or organization that you are responsible for. That is why it is also essential to prioritize spending time with your peers the same way you do with your direct reports.

高管团队经常应用这个概念；然而它适用于任何层级。无论你在产品工程团队、基础设施、SRE 还是 QA 工作，你都需要和你合作的领导群体建立关系。你们一起定义优先级、安排发布、为产品制定战略等，这种协作对你的成功至关重要，因而对你负责的团队或组织的成功也至关重要。这就是为什么优先花时间和同侪在一起也很重要，就像你和下属那样。

How Do You Do That?你怎么做？

Here are some steps to follow:

以下是一些要遵循的步骤：

  • Identify your first team. This is everyone with whom you collaborate to make collective decisions for the team and the organization.识别你的第一团队。这是所有和你合作为团队和组织做集体决策的人。
  • In addition to planning and other project-related meetings, spend time with your peers in one-on-ones on a recurrent basis. This may not be as frequent as with your direct reports, but this will provide you with the required context to understand their perspective when it comes time to make decisions. More important, this is your time to build trust with them.除了计划和其他项目相关会议，定期花时间和同侪一对一。这可能不像和下属那么频繁，但会在做决策时给你理解他们视角所需的上下文。更重要的是，这是你和他们建立信任的时间。
  • Establish how you want to work together. Communicate clearly what you are responsible for, and identify the areas that may overlap.建立你们想怎么一起工作。清楚沟通你负责什么，识别可能重叠的领域。
  • Define how you want to make cross-group decisions and establish the individual and collective goals.定义你想怎么做跨团队决策，建立个人和集体目标。
  • Check those goals periodically.定期检查这些目标。
  • Communicate how you want to receive feedback and ask how they want to receive feedback.沟通你想怎么接收反馈，问他们想怎么接收反馈。
  • Share what you are learning, concerns, and any context that might be helpful to them.分享你在学什么、担忧、以及任何可能对他们有帮助的上下文。

Spending time with your peers across the organization will provide everyone with context and information to make better decisions. This prevents the creation of silos, and fosters the ability to be emphatic when disagreements occur, all leading to a better decision-making process.

花时间和组织里的同侪在一起会给每个人提供上下文和信息做更好的决策。这防止孤岛的产生，培养分歧出现时共情的能力，都导向更好的决策过程。
